newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Clothes maker Shanghai Kaikai to issue B shares.
newsitem.headline: Clothes maker Shanghai Kaikai to issue B shares.

text.p: Clothes maker Shanghai Kaikai Industrial Co Ltd plans to offer 80 million B shares by the end of this year and list them on the Shanghai Stock Exchange in 1997, a company spokesman said on Wednesday.

The firm, which specialises in shirts and woollen sweaters, had been given preliminary approval by the Shanghai Securities Management Office to go ahead with the offer, he told the Hong Kong-based China Securities Bulletin newsletter.
Final approval was subject to the China Securities Regulatory Commission, the official said.
Shanghai Shenyin & Wanguo Securities Co Ltd had been named domestic lead underwriter for the offer, with Shenyin & Wanguo Financial (H.K.) Ltd the international coordinator, he said.
If successful, Kaikai plans to use the B share offer proceeds to renovate production facilities and expand its sales network within mainland China, the official said.
Kaikai has total share capital of 118 million shares, consisting of 71.74 million state shares, 31.26 million legal person shares and 15 million internal staff shares.
Shanghai-based Kaikai marketed most of its Kaikai-brand shirts and sweaters domestically, the official said.

Kaikai, whose net assets are valued at 200 million yuan, forecast after-tax profits of 60 million yuan for 1996, compared with 60.02 million yuan last year and 36.38 million yuan in 1994, under international accounting standards, the official said.
The earnings surge last year was due to its success in expanding sales, he added.
